rv.q: So the phrase 'once-in-a-lifetime opportunity' isn't hyperbole when it comes to Jonathan Kent's thrilling account of this Broadway classic.
Jonathan Kent's perfectly pitched production is worth the 40-year wait.
Nonetheless, it's superior fare and yet another triumph from Chichester Festival Theatre.

For musical theatre actresses the role of Momma Rose is like KING LEAR. In fact to get the chance to play it is even more prestigious. Anyone can have a stab at Lear where as permission to play the lead part in the musical GYPSY is jealously guarded by those who control the performing rights.

It is the character of Rose that is the driving force behind this show and Imelda Staunton is a tour de force in this part. The part is a fabulously written 3 dimensional character that you root for, a driven mother who loves her children yet in the same breath she is the ultimate stage mother who pushes her children away in her hunger for success.

But Momma Rose’s songs are more demanding. Sitting just six rows away from Staunton as she launched into her two act-climaxing solos, ‘Everything’s Coming Up Roses’ and the ferocious and ultimately lump-in-the-throat ‘Rose’s Turn’, was to be at a masterclass in seeing exactly what it is that makes great theatre worth paying astronomical prices for.

Lara Pulver is even better than I remember, watchful and cowed in her early scenes and finally coming out as the burlesque stripper-with-class Gypsy Rose Lee like a butterfly emerging from a chrysalis.

cn.t: Imelda Staunton delivers a career-defining performance as Momma Rose in Jonathan Kent's thrilling revival, marking the show's long-overdue return to the West End after 40 years. Critics hail it as stunning and unmissable.
